label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
# Jonno, here's what happened with the coolroom

Jonno,

You've now asked me about the coolroom roughly nine hundred times and I'm not typing it out with my thumbs after a double. So you're getting a blog post, and everyone else can read along. Hi Mum.

Cup Day, Tuesday the 3rd. I get in at 6.40 and open the coolroom door, and you know that feeling when the air that hits you is just air? Thermometer says 11 degrees. The compressor carked it sometime overnight and I've got no idea when, so I can't tell how long everything's been sitting there warm.

Now picture the day. 140 booked for lunch, set menu, three courses. Raff's off, so it's me running it. You're in London, probably asleep, probably under a nice doona.

First call is Wally from Coldline. Wally can't come till Wednesday because the part has to come down from Sydney. Tuesday is a public holiday, mate, what did I expect.

Second call is Phil. Phil says "just make it work mate." That's the whole call. I want it on the record that "just make it work mate" is what people say instead of having a plan.

So I made the plan, standing in a warm coolroom at quarter to seven. Everything that could be saved went into the two undercounters and the bar fridge. Yes, the bar fridge. There was beef next to the tonic water. Then I went next door and begged Marta, and she gave us half her walk-in, because she's a saint with a head for business (more on that later).

Everything that couldn't be saved went in the bin. About $1800 worth, mostly dairy and the duck legs. I'm fine about the dairy, but I'm still not over the duck legs.

Then Kev, who is the best dishy we've ever had and I won't hear otherwise, takes the old esky up to the servo and comes back with 14 bags of ice. The bloke behind the counter asked him if we were having a party. In a way, yeah.

Then there was the beef, and this is the bit you'd have hated most. Me and Benny had to get 30 kilos of beef shin down the laneway on the milk crate trolley, in the rain. You remember the milk crate trolley and you remember what condition it's in. Halfway down, one of the wheels fell off. It didn't go wobbly, it came off and rolled away. So there's two grown men in the rain, half carrying and half dragging a crate of shin, swearing at each other and at the trolley.

You would've cried. I'm not even having a go, I just know you. London's made you soft. You'd have stood in that laneway and had a little weep, then asked if anyone wanted a flat white.

Anyway, we got it there. And then during service a lady on table 9 asked her waiter if the beef was "free range from the laneway", because she'd watched the whole thing out the window. I've never been so proud and so ashamed at once. Fair play to table 9, that's a better line than anything I came up with all day.

By midday we're cooking 140 covers out of two undercounters, a bar fridge, an esky and a cafe. At 12.15 I had to 86 the panna cotta. It was gone and it wasn't coming back, so dessert became what I told the floor was "affogato with whatever". That's how I briefed it, word for word.

People loved it. They loved it more than the panna cotta, the one that's been on the menu and gets fussed over. We gave them ice cream with coffee on it and whatever else was within reach, and they were scraping the glasses. I don't know what to do with that information and I'm choosing not to think about it.

Here's the bit I didn't expect. It was the best service we've done all year, and I'm not exaggerating. Everyone was locked in. No one whinged, no one went missing, and no one had a sook in the dry store (you've done this). Benny was soaked to the undies and didn't miss a beat. Kev was running ice like it was a paid sport. The floor were unreal. Something about the whole day being cooked from 6.40am meant everyone just got on with it.

I've decided that's the truth about this job. Bistro kitchens run on bar fridges and spite. The coolroom's nice to have, that's all.

A few loose ends for you.

Marta is making us pay her back in what she calls croissant credit. As far as I can work out, I personally owe her about three weeks of staff meal. I haven't seen the maths and I'm scared to ask. She's got us over a barrel and she knows it.

My horse in the sweep was called Ice Cold Lad, I swear to god. I drew that out of the hat on the same day my coolroom was sitting at 11 degrees. He came second last. The universe is taking the piss and not even being subtle about it.

Phil, if you're reading this, we made it work, mate.

So that's the story. Now you can stop messaging me at 3am my time asking "but what happened with the coolroom". You missed the best worst day of the year, and you would've been useless and it would've been great to have you there.

Come home ya flog.

---

I left out whether Wally got it fixed on the Wednesday, since you didn't say. Jonno will ask, so chuck a line in if you want.

reasons: The final note addresses the writing task rather than forming part of the blog post.
